analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation edit to docs/developer/test.md (head lines 673-675). It extends the ModelCheckpointConversationLiveTests description so the report also records delta files and greedy output tokens. It also names the env var DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 as the complete-file baseline. No source, crypto, authorization, attestation or wire behavior changes. The surrounding unchanged text (units :3 and :4) is test-procedure documentation that stays consistent with the existing isolation guidance: the isolated ephemeral cache, `env -i` with only listed variables, and never using production cache roots or keys.

Relevant threat T-041 (SSD prefix-cache at-rest artifacts) is touched only indirectly. The docs reference an incremental/delta checkpoint file mode controlled by DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS. The supplied evidence includes no source for that feature. It is a documentation reference, not proof of a regression, so I record an unverified contract rather than a finding. T-041's detail_hint says nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added to DBK3 metadata or AAD. If the corresponding source PR introduces delta files with new metadata, file naming or AAD fields, or changes the purge, TTL or epoch behavior, that code should be reviewed against T-041 (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, KEK-wipe purge, per-file GCM authentication). The threat model's file list does not name any delta-checkpoint file. It may need an update if delta files add at-rest artifacts. The documented report also records output tokens, but it is synthetic public-prompt test data kept in operator-owned local evidence, with no telemetry path introduced. The docs-only change itself introduces no new attack surface.
